mold

matt helped me with the mold by teaching me how it works, and despite how messy everything was, we were able to get it clamped and would be done overnight.

and then i was gone for the entire school week after that. came back next week tuesday.

this is what it ended up looking like when it was done. super thin (which is what i wanted), but also too brittle. so it broke and became unsalvagable.

because of that, i decided to just not use the mold and instead just friction fit the pcb with the aluminum case (when it gets made), opting for electrical tape to protect the components

case v???

adjusted the tolerances of the case to account for friction fit without the silicone pad, and printed it.

may have been a bit small (could be 3d printer tolerances?) but it didn't fit well, and would flex on the sides causing it to curve in the center

i might just sand it down a bit and test the fit again befofre adjusting anything on fusion.
